output.brief: The evidence points to contaminated brake fluid, not driver technique, Upper Wend hills or the new pads. Northfield Motor Services serviced 13 Eastgate vans between 4 Aug and 12 Sep. Eleven of them used fluid from a bulk drum that had been open since March and had a missing cap. Two vans serviced from a new drum had no complaints. The 11 vans on the bulk drum are exactly the 11 vans behind the 27 complaints. Two of them, retested on 24 Sep, had fluid boiling at about 150°C against 255°C for sealed stock. Water-laden fluid can vaporise on long descents and make the pedal soft. The same drivers had no complaints in other vans on the same hills, and both pad batches were fitted across the affected vans. Northfield recommended rechecking the other vans on 25 Sep, but that email got no reply. Confidence is high, around 90%. Do not discipline the complainers. They reported a real fault, and punishing them would stop reports. Retraining everyone on descent braking is not supported either. This week, pull the 11 bulk-drum vans, including LK-209, and test and renew their fluid from sealed stock. Then check the Calder Road and in-house vans, whose fluid source I haven't seen. Treat the pad switch separately. Squeal reports are confounded by fresh pads.
